triage.reason: Directly relevant to onboarding because it explains why RSS defaults should work before search configuration.

digest.summary: The note argues that RSS should be the default feed substrate because it works without API keys or billing. Search should add depth after the user has already experienced a useful first-run feed.

highlights.text: Search should expand coverage, not decide whether the product works at all.
Defaults should demonstrate the product without becoming generic news.

concepts.definition: A feed mode that works without search credentials, billing, or account setup.
The role of search APIs after baseline feeds already provide value.

structure: Problem: search-key dependency breaks first run
Onboarding: show gathering, reasoning, and capture

hiddenAssumptions: The default RSS sources match the user's interests well enough to demonstrate value.
RSS freshness and availability are reliable enough for first-run use.
potentialIssues: Reddit RSS can be rate-limited or noisy.
Users outside AI/startup interests may need different defaults.
needsVerification: Which default feeds produce the best first-run recommendations.
Whether users notice the difference between RSS-only and search-enhanced mode.
biasIndicators: Prefers immediate local usefulness over exhaustive search coverage.

connections.summary: Both sources prioritize attention triage before organization.
connections.details: The RSS note applies the local-first workflow's principle that defaults should help users judge value before asking them to configure infrastructure.
